news_catalyst.headline: TSMC borrowing from Intel's playbook on integrated design-manufacturing — structural AI chip demand intact
news_catalyst.summary: TSMC continues to be the foundational beneficiary of every GPU, ASIC, and AI chip produced globally. As NVDA, AMD, Apple, AVGO, and hyperscalers all compete for TSMC capacity, the company exercises pricing power that flows directly to margins. The 0.23% move today reflects the stock's role as a high-conviction, low-volatility position in the AI supply chain.

technical.summary: RSI 43.68 and MACD -1.20 suggest near-term momentum is bearish — the stock has been pulling back from recent highs. However, the pullback is on declining volume, which is constructive for accumulation. Recent events show accumulation followed by distribution — contested price zone. Key support at $395-400. Accumulate on continued pullback toward $395.

wyckoff_narrative: Recent alternating accumulation/distribution events suggest price discovery at the $395-430 range. No formal Wyckoff events logged in the current cycle. The stock is likely in Phase B consolidation after prior run-up. A volume dry-up and tight range day near $395-405 would set up an ideal Wyckoff entry.

valuation.summary: DCF appears calculated on TWD (NT dollar) basis — not comparable. Analyst consensus target of $540.20 (34% upside) is the relevant guide. At 18.7x forward PE with 36% revenue growth and 49.9% margins, TSM is attractively valued. Strong buy consensus (1.42) with 34% upside is one of the cleaner risk/reward propositions today.
